title: Tubby Hall and the Ory rhythm section
summary: Russell recalls Tubby Hall's drumming with Dodds and the Ory band's rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah. That's some of the later Defender notes, some things that I probably didn't get. He probably looked through my notes and then went up there and went through a couple of years. We'll copy all this stuff for you. So in any case, there are a few other interviews, people that are dead there like Tubby Hall and Joe Lindsay. Unfortunately, we got very little bit from Tubby Hall. I wanted to apologize on that. He was one of the great drummers, I'm convinced the more I hear of other drummers especially. At that time, I probably didn't pay too much attention to him. I first heard him, oh, maybe half a dozen times on the south side with Johnny Dodd's band. And he wasn't spectacular at all. He just sat there and hardly moved. The one remark that Johnny made, I probably said, well, he's the one who was on the left. He probably said, well, he's the one who was on the Louis Armstrong records. Is that right or something? I wouldn't have hardly known who he was at that time when Johnny first introduced me. And Johnny said, yes, he doesn't, he started it confidentially. He doesn't play as much drums as he used to, you know. So I thought, well, he's not so good or not very great really. And I was more interested in Baby in those days. But then you talk later to Baby and find out Baby admits he got his press role mostly from Tubby Hall. And Tubby went up there, oh, three or four years before most of them, or maybe a couple of years before a lot of the other New Orleans. But he invented it? No, not necessarily. He was one of the first ones that had a good press role, though. But Tubby, I think, went up maybe as, say, something like Natty went up as a cigar maker. He went up as another job, not as a musician at first. He was there a year or so before Oliver and some of the other fellows. But he was undoubtedly one of the great drummers down here even, especially in Chicago, and had a wonderful, simple style. But it wasn't spectacular, and his Baby didn't run around on all the traps. And that one remark, I guess, that Johnny made to me, which Johnny wasn't really trying to knock him. He was just saying he maybe wasn't playing quite the drums he did maybe 10 years before or sometime, or 20 years before. But he was still great. And his brother was one of the great drummers with Kid Ori's band, too. That was the greatest rhythm section I ever heard, I'd say, was that Kid Ori rhythm section with, who's the bass player? Eddie Garland and Bud Scott and Minor Hall, who was the younger brother of Tubby Hall. I guess that's right. I have to stop and think.
